2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A chart author using custom axis label values needs labels to stay aligned with the same ordinal position they supplied, even when some custom values are filtered out because they fall outside the visible axis extent. Right now the formatter callback can receive the wrong index for repeated values because the label-building path looks the position back up from the filtered tick list instead of preserving the mapped position directly.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  When ECharts builds axis labels from `axisLabel.customValues`, the formatter should be called with the actual index of each rendered item in that filtered label sequence, including cases where the same numeric value appears more than once. Authors should be able to rely on formatter logic that branches on the index parameter without seeing duplicated values collapse onto the first matching position.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  For duplicate or repeated custom label values that remain in range, each rendered label keeps its own formatter index and produces the text a user would expect from its own slot in the sequence. Existing axis label rendering behavior, formatter signatures, and label text generation outside this indexing bug remain unchanged.
16	
17	  '

title: 'feat(axis): axisLabel `formatter` can receive its index for working with `customValues`'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Axis label callbacks can format the label value, but authors working with `customValues` also need to know which generated tick they are formatting in order to line up external labels correctly.

  ## Desired outcome

  `axisLabel.formatter` should receive the tick index as an additional argument so formatter logic can work reliably with `customValues`.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A formatter declared as `axisLabel.formatter(value, index)` receives the expected index for each displayed custom tick and can build labels from that position information.

  '
title: 'fix(axis): fix chart does not work when using `customValues` with `formatter` in time axis label'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Time axes can break when authors combine `axisLabel.customValues` with a custom `axisLabel.formatter`, even though that pairing is a reasonable way to build bespoke label sets.

  ## Desired outcome

  Time-axis label generation should support `customValues` and formatter callbacks together without crashing or dropping the axis.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A time axis that uses both `axisLabel.customValues` and `axisLabel.formatter` renders normally and passes the formatter the expected label values.

  '

1	# axislabel-formatter-indexing — implementation plan
2	
3	Requirement: `/workspace/requirements/axislabel-formatter-indexing.yaml`
4	(title: `fix(axis): refactor axisLabel formatter`, category: bugfix; upstream PR mapping
5	`21432.yaml -> axislabel-formatter-indexing.yaml`, see `/workspace/requirements/.rename_map.json`)
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Goal
10	
11	When an axis builds its labels from `axisLabel.customValues`, the user `axisLabel.formatter`
12	callback must be invoked with the **index of the label inside the final, filtered label
13	sequence** (`0, 1, 2, …`), i.e. the position produced by the `map` over the in-extent tick
14	list — *not* `undefined`, and *not* a value looked back up from the tick list (which would
15	collapse repeated values onto the first matching position).
16	
17	Concretely, in `createAxisLabels()` (`/workspace/src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts`) the
18	`customValues` branch currently calls `labelFormatter(tick)` with **no** second argument, so
19	every user formatter for a `value` / `log` / `time` axis receives `index === undefined`. The
20	fix is to thread the `zrUtil.map` iteration index through to `labelFormatter(tick, index)`,
21	so that:
22	
23	* values filtered out because they are outside `axis.scale.getExtent()` do not consume an
24	  index (the first *rendered* label is index `0`);
25	* the same numeric value appearing more than once yields distinct, increasing indices
26	  (`[1, 3, 3, 7]` -> `0, 1, 2, 3`), instead of every duplicate reporting the first matching
27	  position.
28	
29	Everything else (formatter signatures, `rawLabel`, `tickValue`, tick generation, category
30	axis index semantics, non-custom label generation) must stay byte-for-byte identical.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 2. Findings (current code)
35	
36	### 2.1 The defect — `createAxisLabels`, `customValues` branch
37	
38	`/workspace/src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts:123-149`:
39	
40	```ts
41	export function createAxisLabels(axis: Axis, ctx: AxisLabelsComputingContext): {
42	    labels: AxisLabelInfoDetermined[]
43	} {
44	    const custom = axis.getLabelModel().get('customValues');
45	    if (custom) {
46	        const labelFormatter = makeLabelFormatter(axis);
47	        const extent = axis.scale.getExtent();
48	        const tickNumbers = tickValuesToNumbers(axis, custom);
49	        const ticks = zrUtil.filter(tickNumbers, val => val >= extent[0] && val <= extent[1]);
50	        return {
51	            labels: zrUtil.map(ticks, numval => {
52	                const tick = {value: numval};
53	                return {
54	                    formattedLabel: labelFormatter(tick),
55	                    rawLabel: axis.scale.getLabel(tick),
56	                    tickValue: numval,
57	                    time: undefined as ScaleTick['time'] | NullUndefined,
58	                    break: undefined as VisualAxisBreak | NullUndefined,
59	                };
60	            }),
61	        };
62	    }
63	    // Only ordinal scale support tick interval
64	    return axis.type === 'category'
65	        ? makeCategoryLabels(axis, ctx)
66	        : makeRealNumberLabels(axis);
67	}
68	```
69	
70	Line 133 `zrUtil.map(ticks, numval => {` discards the iteration index, and line 136
71	`formattedLabel: labelFormatter(tick),` calls the formatter with a single argument.
72	`ticks` is already the *filtered* list (line 131), so its `map` index is exactly the
73	"index of the rendered item in the filtered label sequence" the requirement asks for.
74	
75	### 2.2 The formatter wrapper already accepts and forwards an index
76	
77	`/workspace/src/coord/axisHelper.ts:231-294` — `makeLabelFormatter()`:
78	
79	```ts
80	export function makeLabelFormatter(axis: Axis): (tick: ScaleTick, idx?: number) => string {
81	```
82	
83	* time branch (`axisHelper.ts:242-247`): `return (axis.scale as TimeScale).getFormattedLabel(tick, idx, parsed);`
84	* string-template branch (`axisHelper.ts:248-256`): ignores `idx` (unchanged by this fix).
85	* function branch, **category** axis (`axisHelper.ts:258-272`): deliberately ignores `idx`
86	  and uses `tick.value - axis.scale.getExtent()[0]` "for back compatibility".
87	* function branch, **non-category** axis (`axisHelper.ts:273-288`):
88	
89	```ts
90	        const scaleBreakHelper = getScaleBreakHelper();
91	        return function (tick: ScaleTick, idx: number) {
92	            ...
93	            return (labelFormatter as AxisLabelValueFormatter)(
94	                getAxisRawValue<false>(axis, tick),
95	                idx,
96	                extra
97	            );
98	        };
99	```
100	
101	So the `idx` plumbing already exists end-to-end; only the call site in
102	`createAxisLabels` fails to supply it.
103	
104	### 2.3 The correct pattern already exists two functions below
105	
106	`/workspace/src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts:277-291` — `makeRealNumberLabels()`:
107	
108	```ts
109	    return {
110	        labels: zrUtil.map(ticks, function (tick, idx) {
111	            return {
112	                formattedLabel: labelFormatter(tick, idx),
113	```
114	
115	i.e. the non-custom numeric path already passes the sequence index; the `customValues`
116	path is the outlier.
117	
118	### 2.4 Public types already declare the index parameter
119	
120	`/workspace/src/coord/axisCommonTypes.ts:239-253`:
121	
122	```ts
123	export type AxisLabelValueFormatter = (
124	    value: number,
125	    index: number,
126	    extra: AxisLabelFormatterExtraParams | NullUndefined,
127	) => string;
128	```
129	
130	(and `AxisLabelCategoryFormatter`, `AxisLabelTimeFormatter` likewise). No type change needed.
131	
132	`/workspace/src/coord/axisCommonTypes.ts:322` declares
133	`customValues?: (number | string | Date)[],` on `AxisLabelBaseOption`.
134	
135	### 2.5 The rendering layer already uses the "rendered sequence index" convention
136	
137	`/workspace/src/component/axis/AxisBuilder.ts:1366` iterates the labels with
138	`each(labels, function (labelItem, index) {` and passes that same `index` to the
139	`axisLabel.color` callback (`AxisBuilder.ts:1433-1449`):
140	
141	```ts
142	                fill: isFunction(textColor)
143	                    ? textColor(
144	                        ...
145	```
146	
147	So after the fix the `formatter` index and the `color` callback index agree for
148	`customValues`, which is the user-visible consistency the requirement describes.
149	
150	### 2.6 Empirically measured current behaviour (jest probe, no repo files touched)
151	
152	Option: `xAxis: {type: 'value', min: 0, max: 10, axisLabel: {customValues: [-5, 1, 3, 3, 7, 20],
153	formatter: (v, i) => i + ':' + v}}`, read back via `axis.getViewLabels()`:
154	
155	```
156	TICKVALUES [1,3,3,7]                                             // filtering already correct
157	FORMATTED  ["undefined:1","undefined:3","undefined:3","undefined:7"]   // BUG: no index
158	CALLS      [[1,null],[3,null],[3,null],[7,null]]                 // (null == undefined via JSON)
159	```
160	
161	Control (same chart without `customValues`) is already correct and must stay correct:
162	
163	```
164	REG FORMATTED ["0:0","1:2","2:4","3:6","4:8","5:10"]
165	REG CALLS     [[0,0],[2,1],[4,2],[6,3],[8,4],[10,5]]
166	```
167	
168	Category axis control (`data: ['a','b','c','d']`, `customValues: ['a','c','a']`) —
169	index comes from the ordinal offset (`axisHelper.ts:268`), *not* from the sequence, and is
170	intentionally left untouched by this fix:
171	
172	```
173	CAT TICKVALUES [0,2,0]
174	CAT FORMATTED  ["0:a","2:c","0:a"]
175	```
176	
177	### 2.7 Related, deliberately out of scope
178	
179	* `/workspace/src/util/time.ts:343-352` (`leveledFormat`) dereferences `tick.time.level`
180	  for function formatters, while the `customValues` branch builds `{value: numval}` with no
181	  `time`. Time axis + `customValues` + function formatter therefore throws today. That is a
182	  *different* requirement (`/workspace/requirements/time-axis-customvalues-formatter.yaml`,
183	  upstream #21352) — do **not** fix it here, and do not write a unit test that exercises it.
184	* `/workspace/src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts:111-121` (`tickValuesToNumbers`) sorts with
185	  the default (lexicographic) comparator and duplicates the first/last entry for time axes.
186	  Out of scope; note only that for a time axis the duplicated first/last entries now each
187	  get their own index, which is the intended "one index per rendered item" semantics.
188	
189	---
190	
191	## 3. Plan (ordered edits)
192	
193	### Edit 1 — pass the map index to the label formatter
194	
195	File: `/workspace/src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts`
196	
197	Anchor (search verbatim; occurs exactly once, at lines 132-143):
198	
199	```ts
200	        return {
201	            labels: zrUtil.map(ticks, numval => {
202	                const tick = {value: numval};
203	                return {
204	                    formattedLabel: labelFormatter(tick),
205	                    rawLabel: axis.scale.getLabel(tick),
206	                    tickValue: numval,
207	                    time: undefined as ScaleTick['time'] | NullUndefined,
208	                    break: undefined as VisualAxisBreak | NullUndefined,
209	                };
210	            }),

212	```

218	            // `index` is the index in the filtered (in-extent) label list, which is what
219	            // `axisLabel.formatter` and `axisLabel.color` callbacks receive elsewhere.
220	            // Caution: it must be preserved from the iteration rather than looked up by
221	            // value (e.g. `zrUtil.indexOf(ticks, numval)`), otherwise repeated custom
222	            // values would all be reported at the first matching position.
223	            labels: zrUtil.map(ticks, (numval, index) => {
224	                const tick = {value: numval};
225	                return {
226	                    formattedLabel: labelFormatter(tick, index),
227	                    rawLabel: axis.scale.getLabel(tick),
228	                    tickValue: numval,
229	                    time: undefined as ScaleTick['time'] | NullUndefined,
230	                    break: undefined as VisualAxisBreak | NullUndefined,

232	            }),

240	  (`/workspace/node_modules/zrender/src/core/util.ts:335-339`), so `index` is
241	  `number | undefined`; `makeLabelFormatter` returns
242	  `(tick: ScaleTick, idx?: number) => string` (`/workspace/src/coord/axisHelper.ts:239`),
243	  so the call type-checks with no cast. The repo's tsconfig does not enable
244	  `strictNullChecks` (`/workspace/tsconfig.json`), so there is no additional narrowing to do.
245	* Keep the arrow-function style — the surrounding lines (`val => val >= extent[0] …`)

366	
367	Why this is deterministic (verified by running the same code from a scratch directory
368	against the unmodified repo):
369	
370	* `axis.getViewLabels()` re-enters `createAxisLabels()` and the `customValues` branch is
371	  **not** cached (the `axisInner` cache is only used by the category-interval paths,
372	  `/workspace/src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts:193-231`), so resetting `calls.length = 0`
373	  immediately before the call captures exactly one formatting pass.
374	* Without the reset, `calls` contains two passes (label estimation + determination) —
375	  `[[1,null],[3,null],…]` repeated twice — so the reset is required.
376	* Pre-fix, `calls` is `[[1, undefined], [3, undefined], [3, undefined], [7, undefined]]` and
377	  `formattedLabel` is `['undefined:1', …]`, so the first test fails before Edit 1 and passes
378	  after it; the second test passes both before and after (regression guard).
379	
380	### Edit 3 (optional, only if a visual case is wanted)
381	
382	`/workspace/test/axis-customTicks.html` already contains a `customValues` + `formatter`
383	case at lines 302-345 (`main5`). No change is required for the fix; adding a duplicate-value
384	case there is optional cosmetic coverage and is **not** part of this plan.
385	
386	---
387	
388	## 4. Tests
389	
390	A unit test is feasible and is specified in full in Edit 2 above:
391	`/workspace/test/ut/spec/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.test.ts`.
392	
393	Helper API actually used (checked against `/workspace/test/ut/core/utHelper.ts` and the
394	existing `/workspace/test/ut/spec/scale/interval.test.ts`):
395	
396	* `import { createChart, getECModel } from '../../core/utHelper';` — `createChart()` takes an
397	  optional `{width, height, theme, opts}` and returns an `EChartsType`; dispose in `afterEach`.
398	* `getECModel(chart).getComponent('xAxis', 0) as CartesianAxisModel` then `.axis` —
399	  `CartesianAxisModel` is the **default** export of
400	  `/workspace/src/coord/cartesian/AxisModel.ts:67`.
401	* `axis.getViewLabels()` (`/workspace/src/coord/Axis.ts:242-247`) returns
402	  `{formattedLabel, rawLabel, tickValue, time, break}[]`; `interval.test.ts:95` uses the same
403	  accessor.
404	* Path alias `@/src/...` -> repo root is configured through
405	  `/workspace/test/ut/tsconfig.json` (`"@/*": ["../../*"]`) plus `moduleNameMapper` in
406	  `/workspace/test/ut/jest.config.cjs`. Both `../../../../src/...` relative imports and
407	  `@/src/...` are used in the existing specs; the plan uses `@/src/...` like
408	  `spec/scale/interval.test.ts`.
409	
410	---
411	
412	## 5. Verification
413	
414	```bash
415	# 1. Type check the source change (whole repo, ~1 min)
416	cd /workspace && npx tsc --noEmit          # === npm run checktype
417	
418	# 2. Run the new spec only
419	cd /workspace && npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs --coverage=false \
420	    test/ut/spec/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.test.ts
421	
422	# 2b. Or by test name
423	cd /workspace && npm run test:single -- "axisLabel_customValues_formatter_index"
424	
425	# 3. Make sure nothing else regressed (full ut suite)
426	cd /workspace && npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs --coverage=false
427	
428	# 4. Lint the touched source file
429	cd /workspace && npx eslint src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts
430	
431	# 5. Apache license header check for the new test file
432	cd /workspace && node build/checkheader.js
433	```
434	
435	Expected: step 2 passes only after Edit 1 (it fails on the unmodified tree with
436	`Expected [[1,0],[3,1],[3,2],[7,3]] / Received [[1,undefined],…]`).
437	
438	Manual/visual (optional): `npm run dev` then open
439	`http://localhost:8080/test/axis-customTicks.html` — `main0`/`main3`/`main5` must render
440	exactly as before (their formatters branch on `value`, not on `index`).
441	
442	---
443	
444	## 6. Risks / open questions
445	
446	1. **Category axes are intentionally not changed.** For `type: 'category'`,
447	   `makeLabelFormatter` (`/workspace/src/coord/axisHelper.ts:258-272`) ignores the `idx`
448	   argument and passes `tick.value - axis.scale.getExtent()[0]` "for back compatibility", so
449	   `customValues: ['a', 'c', 'a']` still yields indices `0, 2, 0`. The requirement talks about
450	   "the same **numeric** value" and about values "filtered out because they fall outside the
451	   visible axis extent", which is the value/log/time path, and the acceptance signal
452	   explicitly asks for *no* other behaviour change — hence the minimal edit.
453	   *If a category case must also report sequence indices*, the (only) additional edit is in
454	   `/workspace/src/coord/axisHelper.ts`, replacing
455	
456	   ```ts
457	            return function (tick: ScaleTick, idx: number) {
458	                // The original intention of `idx` is "the index of the tick in all ticks".
459	   ```
460	   … body …
461	   ```ts
462	                return (labelFormatter as AxisLabelCategoryFormatter)(
463	                    getAxisRawValue<true>(axis, tick),
464	                    tick.value - axis.scale.getExtent()[0],
465	                    null // Using `null` just for backward compat.
466	                );
467	   ```
468	   with `idx != null ? idx : tick.value - axis.scale.getExtent()[0]`. This was checked to be
469	   safe for the other call site that already passes an index for category axes
470	   (`/workspace/src/coord/cartesian/legacyContainLabel.ts:99`, where
471	   `tick.value === categoryScaleExtent[0] + i`, so `idx` and the ordinal offset are equal),
472	   but it *does* change public behaviour for category `customValues`, so it is deliberately
473	   left out unless required.
474	
475	2. **Time axis.** `tickValuesToNumbers` (`axisTickLabelBuilder.ts:111-121`) duplicates the
476	   first and last value for time axes, so a time axis's formatter indices will be
477	   `0..n+1` with the first two and last two entries sharing a value. That is the intended
478	   "one index per rendered item" semantics, and it is the only user-visible index shift
479	   introduced here. Note that time axis + `customValues` + **function** formatter currently
480	   throws in `/workspace/src/util/time.ts:346` (`tick.time.level` on a `time`-less tick);
481	   that is a separate requirement (`time-axis-customvalues-formatter`) — do not test that
482	   combination here, and expect a textual (not semantic) interaction if both changes land in
483	   the same region later.
484	
485	3. **Estimate vs. determine passes.** `AxisBuilder` formats labels twice per render
486	   (`buildAxisLabel` is called with `AxisTickLabelComputingKind.estimate` and
487	   `.determine`, `/workspace/src/component/axis/AxisBuilder.ts:1332-1352`). Formatters with
488	   side effects therefore see two passes; the new test neutralises this by resetting its
489	   call log right before calling `getViewLabels()`. Do not assert on call counts across a
490	   full render.
491	
492	4. **Index type.** `zrUtil.map`'s callback declares `index?: number`; if a future
493	   `strictNullChecks` is enabled the argument stays assignable to
494	   `makeLabelFormatter`'s `idx?: number`, so no cast is needed now or then.
495	
496	5. Nothing else in the repo reads `formattedLabel` in a way that depends on the index
497	   (`getViewLabels` consumers: `/workspace/src/component/axis/AxisBuilder.ts:1352`,
498	   `/workspace/src/component/axis/AngleAxisView.ts:100`,
499	   `/workspace/src/component/timeline/SliderTimelineView.ts:468`,
500	   `/workspace/src/chart/line/LineView.ts:409`), so the blast radius is limited to the text
501	   produced by user formatters on axes that use `axisLabel.customValues`.
